paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The writer talks like a dad who wants his son's heart to be wise, and everything else in this passage hangs on that. He says, "My son, if your heart is wise, my own heart will indeed rejoice" (Proverbs 23:15). Wisdom isn't a trophy to put on a shelf. It's a gift that makes the people who love you glad, and he says to "Invest in truth and never sell it" (Proverbs 23:23).

Then he shows what pulls a heart off course, and notice that every one of them looks good at first. Envying sinners looks like the smart move, and the writer says to "always continue in the fear of the LORD" (Proverbs 23:17). Wine looks its best when it's red and sparkling, but "In the end it bites like a snake and stings like a viper" (Proverbs 23:32). The drinker in the passage doesn't even feel the beating, and he's already asking about the next drink (Proverbs 23:35). That's the trap, friend: something that feels like a treat at the start can end up as the boss of your whole day.

So here's what I want you to take home. Guard your heart before the trap shows up, because the writer says, "guide your heart on the right course" (Proverbs 23:19). Pick the voices you listen to, like the father who gave you life, and the mother you shouldn't despise when she is old (Proverbs 23:22). And hang onto the promise under the whole passage: "For surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off" (Proverbs 23:18). The wise aren't done talking yet, so keep your ears open!
